description: Library L12 (P7+P8). Lumbar strain after a pickup collision, PCP, physical therapy with Waddell lines charted four ways (two clean negations, a positive count with inconsistent effort, a mixed-side sentence and a contrast sentence with 'symptom magnification'), a 49-day gap, and a carrier records-review letter received after the demand that restates the same Waddell lines and offers an opinion. Clean negations must not flag; every other credibility sentence must (D-043). The tool never concludes malingering and never adopts the carrier's opinion.

totals.accept_all_reason: Hand-verified against the records: ED charge $2,780 + itemized statement lines $210 + $2,320 + $480 = $5,790; the $145 fee schedule is a rate. D-060 (default-deny): the three statement lines (initial evaluation, treatment visits 1 through 16, functional capacity evaluation) state no date of service, so they are not itemized service lines and are listed under Amounts not totaled. Accepting the acceptable lines one at a time gives $2,780.00 (the ED charge); $5,790.00 is reached after the paralegal reads the statement and reclassifies the three lines.

must_not_flag.statement: No gap flag for the 14, 14, 21, 21 and 14-day intervals; the carrier letter (record 9) and the statement (record 10) are not gap endpoints.
Record 4 charts '0/5 Waddell signs.' alone: a clean negation (D-043 allow-list) must not flag.
Record 5 charts 'No Waddell signs.' and 'Good effort.': clean negations must not flag.

must_not.statement: Concludes malingering, exaggeration, dishonesty or secondary gain, or says a Waddell count shows the pain is not genuine; the records chart signs and effort only.
bad_examples: Waddell signs show the pain is not genuine.
good_examples: The functional capacity evaluation of 2026-04-20 charts Waddell 3/5 positive; effort inconsistent.
Carrier records review quotes the FCE: Waddell 3/5 and inconsistent effort.
PT note of 2026-03-09 charts 0/5 Waddell signs.

must_not.statement: Uses the words malingering, feigning, faking, exaggerating or secondary gain in the tool's own text.
good_examples: Symptom magnification is the PT's wording.

must_not.statement: States the carrier reviewer's opinion as fact (self-limited strain, treatment not necessary, MMI) instead of attributing it to the carrier's letter.
bad_examples: Treatment after 04/20/2026 was not reasonable or necessary.
She reached maximum medical improvement on 04/20/2026.
good_examples: The carrier's records-review letter opines treatment after 04/20/2026 was not reasonable or necessary.
Carrier reviewer (did not examine the claimant) opines the findings are consistent with a self-limited lumbar strain.

must_not.statement: Adds, averages or trends Waddell counts across dates, or treats a positive count as proof of non-organic pain.
bad_examples: Waddell signs totaled 3 across her visits.
The average Waddell score was 1.5 out of 5.
A positive Waddell count proves the pain is non-organic.
good_examples: Waddell signs negative on the left and positive on the right, as charted on 2026-05-04.

must_not.statement: Adds the fee-schedule rate to the charges or sums the statement lines into a figure the records do not state (values 5,935 / 6,270 / 2,925 / 3,010).

notes: Library packet (T-079); scenario shapes: P7 + P8 in research/case-library-sources-v2.md; layouts in research/record-formats.md. All names, providers, places, dates and amounts are invented.

Hand arithmetic: 02-09 to 02-23 = 14; to 03-09 = 5 + 9 = 14; to 03-30 = 21; to 04-20 = 1 + 20 = 21; to 05-04 = 10 + 4 = 14; to 06-22 = 27 + 22 = 49 (flag). The carrier letter (07-15) and statement (07-31) are non-encounters.

Credibility sentences (D-043): clean negations in records 4 and 5 (must not flag); a positive count with inconsistent effort (record 6), a mixed-side sentence and a contrast sentence (record 7), and the carrier's three restatements (record 9) flag. Three further dismissable non-credibility flags (P1, K8, K9) exercise the dismissal-pattern guard (T-089): the tool must never learn to auto-dismiss credibility flags.
Litigation-stage variant (not in this packet): the same wording in a post-suit TRCP 204 exam report.
